item.title: If Trump Strikes Iran: Mapping the Oil Disruption Scenarios
item.description: In last summer’s Twelve-Day War, energy supplies were largely spared. But in a potential new round of fighting between the United States and Iran, energy supply disruptions and resulting price spikes are more likely.

item.title: Transnistria: A Conflict Unfrozen but Not Thawed
item.description: For the first time in three decades, there is clear and significant momentum toward Transnistrian reintegration, but converting this moment into a permanent solution requires vision, substantial financial resources, and delicate diplomacy.

item.title: States Weekly: February 18, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers February 18, 2026.

item.title: Trump Discovers Multilateralism
item.description: This week, Bill Reinsch discusses the Forum on Resource Geostrategic Engagement (FORGE), and how the Trump administration is using multilateralism despite its preference for unilateralism

item.title: Critical Minerals Ministerial Introduces New International Cooperation Strategy
item.description: At the inaugural Critical Minerals Ministerial, 55 foreign ministers convened to advance minerals security through new bilateral and plurilateral frameworks, marking a shift toward coordinated, market-shaping efforts to stabilize prices and strengthen allied supply chains.

item.title: Satellite Imagery Analysis of China’s Alleged 2020 Nuclear Test at Lop Nur
item.description: New claims of supercritical testing at Lop Nur suggest China is improving the science that supports its nuclear arsenal. The United States should proceed carefully to avoid a renewed era of unrestrained nuclear testing.

item.title: After Bangladesh Votes: Stability Will Be Earned Through Delivery, Not Declarations
item.description: A clear electoral mandate has emerged in Bangladesh yet mandates alone do not guarantee stability. The incoming BNP government must prove that political change can deliver security, economic relief, and institutional stability—not just a new set of leaders.

item.title: Golden Dome One Year In
item.description: A year after President Trump’s executive order to create Golden Dome for America, CSIS experts review what has been accomplished over the last year, frame the way ahead, and explore the future of next-generation missile defense.

item.title: Understanding Federal Equity Investments in Strategic Companies
item.description: The Trump administration has marked a significant shift in U.S. industrial policy. The U.S. government is now a direct shareholder in private companies, moving beyond traditional market-based approaches to competitiveness that have marked U.S. policy in the postwar period.
